title: Three bootstrappers crash the party
lede: Most of this week's movement came from two places: a scoring change that finally gives credit to companies that grew without venture money, and job boards we can now read. Here is what really changed, and what only looks like it did.

items.name: Column
items.why: Column is a bootstrapped, founder-owned bank. Under the new self-funded rule, a company that grows without a VC round now gets funding credit instead of a zero. That alone lifted Column two zones and into the 100.

items.name: PLAUD
items.why: PLAUD is profitable with no disclosed VC round, so it earns the same bootstrapped credit. Add 51 open roles and it lands in Sprint.

items.name: DeepInfra
items.why: Nothing changed at DeepInfra. What changed is that its job board became readable this week. Open roles went from unreadable (counted as 0) to 18, and that hiring signal moved it up to Sprint.

items.name: Loop
items.why: A real hiring push. Open roles more than doubled, from 23 to 51, which tipped Loop into Sprint.

items.name: Viktor
items.why: The score slipped half a point and Viktor dropped a zone. Hiring barely moved (31 → 29 open roles), so read this as a small cooling, not a stall. On a list this tight, half a point is worth about 80 places.

items.name: Simile
items.why: Same story: half a point lower, one zone down. Open roles went from 10 to 9.

items.name: Runpod
items.why: Runpod lost half a point and moved from Race to Tempo, with open roles down from 30 to 26.

sections.heading: Pushed out, not downgraded
sections.body: Cresta, n8n, Owner, Scribe and Listen Labs all held their 4.5 Race score. They slipped below #100 only because new high-ranking additions took spots above them. Same pace, more company.

spotlight.label: Early-stage pick of the week
spotlight.name: Harbor
spotlight.tagline: Insurance for AI agents: find every agent a company runs, measure its risk, block bad decisions, and insure what's left.

facts.v: Harbor inventories a company's AI agents, scores each one's operational, security and regulatory risk (mapped to NIST AI RMF and the EU AI Act), blocks decisions that break the company's own rules before they go through, and re-measures whenever a model, tool or data source changes. The risk that remains gets insured: hallucinations, action errors, data leakage, bias, contract failures.
Founded in 2026 and out of stealth on Oct 13. First customers are banks and insurers in the US, Europe and Latin America. No revenue, customer counts or premiums disclosed yet.
$10M seed led by Base10, Abstract and 8VC, with NFX, Restive, Innovation Endeavors, Kibo Ventures, Masia and MVP Ventures.

Four Spanish founders out of Stanford: Jesús Santos (CEO; ex-Morgan Stanley, McKinsey, Crossmint), Daniel Elechiguerra (ex-McKinsey, Citadel), Cristian Bartolomé (2x founder, Pulsar and Factored) and Luis Botín (AI safety research). Former Aon EMEA CEO Eduardo Dávila advises.
Underwriting a brand-new risk with no loss history is unproven. Watch whether carriers and reinsurers take it on.
Warm-up (2.5), Unproven distance: a launch round, too early to rate.

spotlight.why: AI opened a whole new category here. As companies roll out agents that move money, sign contracts and talk to customers, something will go wrong, and right now nobody clearly owns that risk. I see it building agents ourselves: there's always the chance one does the wrong thing at scale. Guardrails and governance are going to be required, and Harbor is building both the controls and the insurance behind them.
